title: Transition to Biomedical Science & Genetics

starterQuestions.q: Outline the three core units comprising the AAQ Human Biology qualification.
starterQuestions.a: 1. Genetics & Gene Expression; 2. Biomedical Techniques (F173); 3. Fundamentals of Human Biology (F170).

starterQuestions.q: What is the assessment distinction between mandatory exam units and NEA units?
starterQuestions.a: Exam units are externally assessed via timed terminal papers; NEA units are internally completed coursework tasks validated by OCR moderation.

starterQuestions.q: What is a COSHH assessment in a biomedical teaching laboratory?
starterQuestions.a: Control of Substances Hazardous to Health: systematic identification of hazardous reagents, exposure routes, and necessary risk mitigations.

starterQuestions.q: Name three standard personal protective equipment (PPE) requirements for diagnostic reagents.
starterQuestions.a: Lab coat (fastened), safety spectacles/goggles, and nitrile protective gloves.

starterQuestions.q: What core genetic concept connects Unit 1 to the upcoming Genetics unit?
starterQuestions.a: Phenotypic variation arising from the complex interplay of polygenic inheritance and environmental influences.

starterQuestions.q: Why is a strict NEA task schedule essential for Year 12 learners?
starterQuestions.a: NEA tasks require multi-week practical optimization, clinical record tracking, and sequential milestone submission deadlines.

courseName: OCR Level 3 Cambridge Advanced National (AAQ) in Human Biology

objectives.knowledge: Understand the linear three-unit curriculum structure: Genetics → Biomedical Techniques → Fundamentals of Human Biology.
objectives.application: Apply COSHH regulations and risk assessments to hazardous diagnostic reagents, stains, and biological specimens.
objectives.evaluation: Evaluate the assessment milestones and bridge foundational knowledge into the upcoming Genetics and Phenotypic Variation unit.

terminology.def: Sequential course progression ensuring prerequisite molecular genetics concepts precede applied biomedical laboratory techniques.
Internally assessed, OCR-moderated practical and research coursework contributing directly to the final qualification grade.
UK legal framework mandating employers and schools to control health hazards from hazardous chemical substances.
Observable physical and biochemical differences among individuals resulting from genetic alleles, environment, and epigenetics.
